# Proof Summary: Marriage of Amelia Frances Gioiello

## Conclusion

Amelia Frances Gioiello married Stanley Datchuk on 20 August 1955 in Niles, Trumbull County, Ohio. The marriage is documented by Ohio Marriage License Application and Certificate No. 43517, Trumbull County Probate Court — an original civil record bearing direct primary evidence from three independent sets of informants: the parties themselves (sworn application), Father Nicholas Anioli, C.P.P.S. (officiating priest's certification), and Judge Sydney W. Jones (Trumbull County Probate Court, licensing and recording).

## Primary Evidence

Ohio, County Marriage License Application and Certificate No. 43517, Trumbull County, Ohio; Stanley Datchuk and Amelia Frances Gioiello, married 20 August 1955; image, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G9WJ-M3P : accessed 28 July 2026), citing Trumbull County Probate Court, Warren, Ohio. [Original source; primary information; direct evidence.]

The application, sworn by both parties on 13 August 1955 before Deputy Clerk Cyril Sherman, names the groom as **Stanley Datchuk**, age 27 as of 14 September 1954, residing at 530 Saline, Niles, Ohio, born in Niles, Ohio, occupation "Opp. Garage," son of Nikolas Datchuk and Sarah Frymarchuk (maiden). The bride is named as **Amelia Frances Gioiello**, age 19 as of 16 November 1954, residing at 819 Henry Street, Niles, Trumbull County, Ohio, born in Niles, Ohio, occupation Clerk, daughter of Joseph Gioiello and Lena Mauro (maiden). Neither party had been previously married. The marriage was solemnized on 20 August 1955 by Father Nicholas Anioli, C.P.P.S., in Niles, Ohio, and recorded by the Probate Court on 22 August 1955 as Certificate No. 43517.

## Corroborating Evidence

"Ohio, County Marriages, 1789-2016", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q297-LTGC : Mon Jan 13 08:11:34 UTC 2025), Entry for Stanley Datchuk and Amelia Frances Gioiello, 20 Aug 1955. [Derivative source; primary information; direct evidence.]

This county marriage index entry independently corroborates the parties' names, the marriage date of 20 August 1955, and the Trumbull County, Ohio jurisdiction. The bride's parents are named as Joseph Gioiello and Lena Mauro; the groom's parents as "Geo Datchuk" and "Sarah Mynarchyk."

## Resolution of Discrepancies

**Bride's mother's surname (Mauro vs. Manro).** The project tree previously recorded the bride's mother (GCT1-CC7) as "Lena Manro." Both the county index and the original certificate record the maiden surname as "Mauro." The original certificate, in which the bride supplied the information under oath and the mother signed the consent section as "Lena Gioiello," constitutes primary evidence. "Manro" in the tree was a data-entry error; "Mauro" is the correct form.

**Groom's father's given name (Nikolas vs. Geo).** The county index names the groom's father as "Geo Datchuk." The original sworn application names him "Nikolas Datchuk." "Geo" (commonly an abbreviation for George) is not a recognizable short form of Nikolas; this is a transcription error in the index. The sworn application prevails. Tree person I2 has been updated to reflect "Nikolas Datchuk."

**Groom's mother's maiden name (Frymarchuk vs. Mynarchyk).** The index records "Sarah Mynarchyk"; the original sworn application records "Sarah Frymarchuk." Both forms appear to be transliterations of a Ukrainian-origin surname. The sworn original certificate is the stronger evidence; "Frymarchuk" is the concluded form, with the index variant noted.

**Collateral birth year discrepancies.** The original certificate states the bride was 19 years of age as of 16 November 1954, implying a birth year of approximately 1935 — conflicting with the tree entry of 1936. The groom's stated age implies a birth year of approximately 1927, conflicting with the index entry of approximately 1933. These are collateral to the marriage question; the marriage date of 20 August 1955 is uncontested. The birth-year conflicts are noted for future research: a Trumbull County birth certificate for Amelia Frances Gioiello and a birth record for Stanley Datchuk would resolve them.

## Research Scope

Searches included the FamilySearch Ohio, County Marriages 1789-2016 index; the original marriage certificate image; US census records for 1900, 1910, and 1920 (appropriate negatives given the subject's mid-1930s birth year); and a FAN search on Joseph Gioiello in the 1880 US Census. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive.

## GPS Assessment

All five GPS components are satisfied: (1) research declared reasonably exhaustive; (2) complete, accurate citations supplied; (3) evidence from both sources classified and correlated; (4) the Mauro/Manro discrepancy and index transcription errors resolved with explicit reasoning; (5) this soundly reasoned written conclusion. The conclusion is stated at the **proved** tier. The original civil marriage certificate — with sworn primary information from the parties, the officiating priest, and the Probate Court — is the definitive documentary record of the marriage. No contrary evidence was found.
